terminal_result.message: Initialized a probe-fed circular microstrip radiator configured for 3.3 GHz on Rogers RO4003C substrate. Note that geometric inspection flags warnings regarding the probe feed contacting the ground plane and discrete port terminals attaching across connected conductive geometry, which is characteristic of the default idealized coaxial probe pin model prior to detailed via/coaxial clearance definition.

Initialized a center-fed dipole antenna for the 915 MHz ISM band (0.915 GHz). The design features copper cylindrical arms of length 76.18 mm each with a 1.09 mm wire radius, separated by a 3.28 mm feed gap (total length 155.63 mm) and excited via a 50-ohm discrete port. Geometric and excitation checks passed with no warnings.

The 2x2 inset-fed microstrip patch array has been built for 5.2 GHz on FR4 substrate. Note the engineering warnings: in this canonical recipe geometry, the feed lines for the upper row elements extend across the lower row elements to reach the board edge, resulting in conductor overlap between rows, shared excitation segments, and coincident discrete port placements.

Axial-mode helical antennas are not supported by the installed antenna recipes. Currently supported antenna families are rectangular inset-fed patch (inset_patch_v2), probe-fed circular patch (circular_patch_v1), and center-fed dipole (dipole_v1).
A 4 mm by 1.5 mm rectangular slot located 6 mm to the left of the patch center has been cut from the radiating patch conductor.

Could you please clarify the exact center position or alignment for the 2.5 mm radius circular conductor (for example, whether it should be centered at the upper-right corner of the patch, or at a specific coordinate along the top or right edge)?

Successfully created and subtracted the two circular cuts from the radiating patch conductor: radius 1.8 mm centered at x = -7 mm, y = 0 mm, and radius 2.2 mm centered at x = 5 mm, y = 0 mm relative to the patch center. All geometric checks passed with zero warnings.

The array has been expanded to a 1x3 configuration with three elements in a single row, and the circular aperture composition has been applied to all radiating patch elements. Conductor support and clearance checks completed with no warnings.
The existing circular aperture has been increased to a radius of 4.25 mm by updating the parameter in the existing composed feature, without adding any additional cuts.
The repeated aperture has been successfully shifted 4 mm toward positive x on every element, measured relative to each element's center.

The existing rectangular slot width has been updated to 8.0 mm, keeping its 1.0 mm height and centered location intact on the patch conductor. Geometric and excitation integrity checks completed with no warnings.
The design currently has two cutouts: a circular slot (composition_1) and a rectangular slot (composition_2). Which cutout would you like to remove, or would you like to remove both?
The antenna element has been replicated into a 1x4 linear array (single row of four elements) with 0.6 free-space wavelength spacing along the horizontal axis.

The antenna currently has a physically realized 'independent_ports' excitation strategy with four individual discrete feed ports (feed network: 'independent'):

- Port 1 (excitation_1_1): Assigned to element (1, 1), 50 Ω discrete port between ground (z = 0 mm) and the feed line (z = 1.6 mm) at x ≈ -33.65 mm, y ≈ -48.05 mm.
- Port 2 (excitation_1_2): Assigned to element (1, 2), 50 Ω discrete port between ground (z = 0 mm) and the feed line (z = 1.6 mm) at x ≈ 33.65 mm, y ≈ -48.05 mm.
- Port 3 (excitation_2_1): Assigned to element (2, 1), 50 Ω discrete port between ground (z = 0 mm) and the feed line (z = 1.6 mm) at x ≈ -33.65 mm, y ≈ 19.25 mm.
- Port 4 (excitation_2_2): Assigned to element (2, 2), 50 Ω discrete port between ground (z = 0 mm) and the feed line (z = 1.6 mm) at x ≈ 33.65 mm, y ≈ 19.25 mm.

All four ports are geometrically attached to their respective local inset feed strips and the ground plane, with realization status 'realized'.

The array has been successfully reconfigured to a 1x5 linear array (1 row, 5 columns) while retaining independent port excitation across all five elements. All geometric and excitation checks completed with no warnings.

The model currently realizes an independent discrete port excitation for each element (strategy: independent_ports):

• Physical Ports: 4 individual 50 Ω discrete ports (port_1 through port_4), assigned respectively to array elements (1,1), (1,2), (2,1), and (2,2).
• Port Geometry: Vertical discrete ports connecting from the ground plane (z = 0 mm) to the local microstrip feed conductor (z = 1.6 mm) at the input of each patch.
• Element Feed Geometry: Each patch element features an integrated inset-fed microstrip line (feed width = 3.0 mm, inset depth = 8.64 mm, gap = 1.0 mm).
• Feed Network: There is no shared corporate or series transmission-line feed network physically modeled; each element is excited independently.

Review completed for benchmark_warning_patch_overlap:

1. Geometry Concern (Warning): A significant support overhang is present. The unioned cylinder feature ('overhang_union_tool') centered at x = 20 mm with radius 18 mm extends to x = 38 mm, overhanging the substrate edge (substrate boundary x_max = 25.62 mm) by approximately 12.38 mm, leaving ~309.4 mm² of conductor outside the dielectric support footprint.

2. Excitation Status: Excitation is configured as a realized single_element_feed with discrete Port 1 attached between the microstrip feed strip and ground at the board boundary. Geometric port mapping is consistent, though full-wave resonance, impedance match, and return loss are not evaluated by these geometry checks.

Resolution of the conductor overhang is recommended before final export.

Installed engineering checks evaluated conductor contact clearance, excitation consistency, port attachment distinctness, and substrate containment. Two warning issues were identified:

1. Conductor Contact (feed & ground): `element_1_probe` contacts `ground` at z = 0 mm without an antipad/clearance opening.
2. Port Attachment Distinctness: Because the probe contacts both the patch and the ground plane, discrete `port_1` has both terminals geometrically attached to the same contiguous conductor body.

Substrate containment and port terminal attachments are otherwise valid. Note that these checks evaluate geometric relationships only and do not establish RF match, resonance, bandwidth, or full-wave validity.

Array Assessment:

1. Detected Issue Needing Attention:
- Substrate Support Overhang (Warning): In elements [1, 3] and [2, 3], the composed cylinder union features (`overhang_union_r1c3_tool` and `overhang_union_r2c3_tool`) extend beyond the substrate boundary by approximately 12.38 mm (~309.4 mm² outside support area). Increasing `board_margin_mm` or repositioning/resizing the composed feature is necessary to keep all conductive elements on the substrate.

2. Remaining Limitations:
- Geometric Checks Only: The checks verify physical layout consistency but do not validate RF performance, resonance, input impedance, coupling, or radiation efficiency.
- Polygonal Boundary Approximation: Curved cylinder boundaries are discretized, causing port attachment and internal union clearance for some terminals to report an 'unknown' status rather than definitive contact.
- Excitation Intent vs. Synthesis: The array currently uses 6 idealized independent discrete vertical ports; no physical corporate or series distribution network is modeled.

The present element pitch along both array principal axes (rows and columns) is 0.55 λ₀ (free-space wavelengths). At 2.45 GHz (λ₀ ≈ 122.36 mm), this corresponds to a physical element spacing of approximately 67.30 mm. Note that this value reflects the canonical array spacing and ideal periodic principal-plane geometry; it does not model mutual coupling, finite-array truncation, or full-wave electromagnetic effects.

Analytical grating-order evaluation for a 35° scan angle in the principal planes completed:

• Configuration: 2.45 GHz with row and column element spacing of 0.55 λ₀ (67.30 mm).
• Visible Grating Orders: 0 visible non-zero integer spatial orders along either principal axis (row or column) at a 35° scan angle (sin(35°) ≈ 0.574, while the first grating order m = -1 falls at sin(θ) ≈ -1.245, outside visible space).

Assumptions and Limitations: This analytical check evaluates ideal periodic array principal-plane conditions with progressive phase steering. It does not account for finite array edge effects, mutual coupling, element radiation pattern shaping, feed network amplitude/phase errors, substrate surface-wave coupling, or full-wave electromagnetic behavior.

Installed rectangular-patch analytical baseline (at 2.45 GHz, εr = 4.4, h = 1.6 mm):
- Effective dielectric constant (ε_eff): 4.081
- Fringing extension (ΔL): 0.739 mm
- Estimated patch width: 37.234 mm (canonical: 37.2343 mm)
- Estimated patch length: 28.809 mm (canonical: 28.8093 mm)

What this estimate cannot prove:
- The radiator contains composed slot geometry (a 3.0 mm radius center circular slot) and inset feed notches, none of which are modeled or accounted for by the closed-form baseline.
- It does not account for slots, loading, feed perturbations, or finite ground plane effects.
- It does not calculate or establish impedance matching, return loss, bandwidth, radiation efficiency, realized gain, or polarization.
- It is not a full-wave electromagnetic simulation; satisfying the conventional closed-form rectangular dimensions does not guarantee resonance or RF validity for the slotted radiator.

Comparison with the free-space half-wave baseline at 2.45 GHz (lambda_0 = 122.36 mm):

- Modeled Dipole Dimensions:
  * Total length (tip-to-tip span): 58.123 mm (0.475 lambda_0)
  * Arm lengths: 28.450 mm each (0.233 lambda_0 each)
  * Feed gap: 1.224 mm (0.010 lambda_0)
  * Conductor diameter: 0.816 mm (0.0067 lambda_0)
  * Total conductor length: 56.899 mm (0.465 lambda_0)

- Baseline Reference:
  * Free-space half-wave reference (lambda_0 / 2): 61.182 mm
  * Quarter-wave arm reference (lambda_0 / 4): 30.591 mm
  * Difference: -3.059 mm (-5.00% relative to lambda_0 / 2)

- Analytical Limitations:
  1. The lambda_0 / 2 baseline is an analytical reference, not a predicted resonant dimension.
  2. Real resonance is influenced by finite conductor diameter, feed gap capacitance, end effects, and surrounding structures.
  3. This baseline check does not compute input impedance, match/return loss, radiation pattern, efficiency, gain, or balun performance.
  4. Full-wave electromagnetic simulation is required to validate actual RF resonance and impedance matching.

terminal_result.message: You have asked to remember a long-term goal for circular polarization (recorded as future intent: target_polarization = "circular", from your instruction: "Long term I want circular polarization"). The current physical design remains the linearly polarized 2.4 GHz inset-fed patch array.

The active size constraint retained in project memory is:
- Maximum board width (`max_board_width_mm`): 90.0 mm (revised from the initial 72 mm limit).

Currently Realized Excitation:
- Strategy: Independent ports (realization status: realized).
- Physical Ports: 6 discrete 50 Ω ports (port_1 through port_6) are physically attached, each driving one corresponding element across the 2x3 patch array.
- Feed Network: Independent local feeds per element.

Feed Goal (Project Intent):
- A corporate distribution network is recorded as a future project goal for the array, while keeping separate discrete element ports physically active for now (corporate feed physical synthesis is currently not installed).
The requested spiral antenna family is not installed as a validated recipe.
Could you clarify which feature you would like to remove: the circular slot on the left (composition_1) or the rectangular slot near the center (composition_2)?
Could you please specify the radius and offset coordinates (x and y offsets relative to the patch center) for the circular aperture?
What feed probe offset (in mm) would you like to set to place the probe outside the patch radiator (current patch radius is 21.05 mm)?

The circular microstrip radiator at 3.3 GHz on Rogers RO4003C is already created and validated. The current design uses the circular_patch_v1 recipe with frequency_ghz=3.3 and substrate material Rogers RO4003C. All geometry, ports, and excitation are realized.

A basic center-fed dipole for the 915 MHz ISM band is already created and validated. The current design uses the dipole_v1 recipe with frequency_ghz = 0.915 GHz, arm_length_mm ≈ 76.18 mm, conductor_radius_mm ≈ 1.09 mm, and feed_gap_mm ≈ 3.28 mm. All validation stages pass and the engineering checks report only informational findings (no warnings).

The requested FR4 inset-fed patch at 5.2 GHz as a 2×2 array already exists in the current working design. The design uses the inset_patch_v2 recipe with FR4 substrate, frequency_ghz=5.2, array_rows=2, array_columns=2, and element_spacing_lambda=0.55. All geometry, ports, and array configuration have been created and validated.

Axial-mode helical antennas are not supported by the installed recipes. Available antenna families are rectangular inset patch, circular patch, and center-fed dipole. No recipe or modifier can create a helical antenna geometry.

The requested 4 mm × 1.5 mm rectangular slot centered 6 mm left of the patch center already exists in the current design. Parameters slot_width_mm (4 mm) and slot_height_mm (1.5 mm) were created, the boolean tool slot_left_tool was placed at x = -6 mm in the patch-local frame, and the subtract operation slot_left_subtract was applied to element_1_1_patch. No further action is needed.

The requested 2.5 mm radius circular conductor is already attached to the upper-right edge of the radiating patch. The current design (revision 1) includes the parameter `attach_radius_mm` (2.5 mm), the geometry tool `upper_right_circle_tool` positioned at the patch's upper-right corner (center_1 = patch_width_mm/2, center_2 = patch_length_mm/2), and the boolean union `upper_right_circle_union` that merges it with `element_1_1_patch`. No further action is needed.

The requested circular cuts are already present in the current design. The design contains two circular slots subtracted from the patch: slot_1_tool with radius 1.8 mm at x=-7 mm (center_1=-7) and slot_2_tool with radius 2.2 mm at x=5 mm (center_1=5), both relative to the patch center. These were created in the previous step and are part of the composed feature composition_1.

The design already has three elements in one row (array_columns=3, array_rows=1) and the existing center-slot aperture (composition_1) is applied to all radiating patches (scope: all). No further changes are required.
The OpenRouter Nemotron planner returned an invalid plan twice: The LLM planner returned malformed JSON.
The agent exhausted its accepted action-batch budget.
The rectangular opening width (rect_slot_width_mm) is already set to 8 mm in the current design. No change is required.
There are two cutouts (slots) on the patch: a left circular slot (composition_1) and a right rectangular slot (composition_2). Which cutout would you like to remove?

The current design already implements a horizontal row of four elements with 0.6 free-space-wavelength spacing. The array configuration shows 1 row, 4 columns, and element_spacing_lambda = 0.6 (73.42 mm at 2.45 GHz). All four patch elements, feeds, and ports are present and validated.

The current design physically realizes an **independent-ports excitation strategy** across the 2×2 array. Each of the four patch elements has its own discrete vertical port (port_1 through port_4) that connects the patch feed region to the ground plane through the substrate. All four ports are realized and assigned one-to-one to the elements:

- Element (1,1) → port_1 (excitation_1_1)
- Element (1,2) → port_2 (excitation_1_2)
- Element (2,1) → port_3 (excitation_2_1)
- Element (2,2) → port_4 (excitation_2_2)

The feed network is "independent" (no corporate or series feed synthesis). The excitation strategy is recorded as "independent_ports" with realization_status "realized", and the engineering checks confirm four distinct geometric port segment groups, each attached to its respective patch feed and ground.

The current design already has a 1×5 array (array_rows=1, array_columns=5) with independent excitation. The excitation strategy is 'independent_ports' with five discrete ports (port_1 through port_5), each assigned to one of the five elements. No changes are needed.

The current design uses **independent discrete ports** (strategy: `independent_ports`, realization_status: `realized`). Each of the four array elements has its own vertical discrete port connecting the local inset feed strip to the ground plane:

- **Port 1** → element (1,1) at x = -33.65 mm, y = -48.05 mm
- **Port 2** → element (1,2) at x = +33.65 mm, y = -48.05 mm
- **Port 3** → element (2,1) at x = -33.65 mm, y = +19.25 mm
- **Port 4** → element (2,2) at x = +33.65 mm, y = +19.25 mm

Each port is a 50 Ω discrete port with its positive terminal on the copper feed strip (z = substrate_thickness_mm = 1.6 mm) and negative terminal on the ground plane (z = 0). The feed network is **independent** (no corporate or series feed synthesis). All four ports are physically realized and geometrically attached to their respective feed strips and the ground plane.

Review complete. The antenna has one geometry warning and one excitation concern:

1. **Geometry Warning (Support Overhang)**: The `overhang_union_tool` (a copper cylinder added via composition) extends 12.38 mm beyond the substrate footprint, with 309.4 mm² of conductor area outside the support tolerance. The cylinder (center x=20 mm, radius=18 mm) reaches x=38 mm in patch-local coordinates, while the substrate only extends to x≈25.6 mm (half board width). This overhang may affect fabrication and electromagnetic behavior.

2. **Excitation Concern (Port Attachment Uncertain)**: The positive port terminal (at patch-local 0, -21.4 mm, z=1.6 mm) cannot be reliably determined as attached to the radiating patch conductor. The negative terminal attaches to the ground plane. This geometric ambiguity does not imply an impedance mismatch but warrants verification in the solver.

All other checks (conductor clearances, union contacts, substrate containment for ground, port distinctness) are informational with no violations.

Engineering checks completed on the current circular patch design. Two warning-level findings were identified:

1. **Port terminals on same conductor component** (group eng-group-v1-cb92c620...): Both the positive and negative terminals of port_1 attach to the same geometrically connected conductor component (the probe feed connects patch to ground). This makes the excitation geometrically suspicious for a discrete port.

2. **Probe–ground contact** (group eng-group-v1-cfb9d3cd...): The probe feed cylinder contacts the ground plane within geometric tolerance (XY overlap ~1.13 mm², zero clearance). This is expected for a probe-fed patch where the probe penetrates the substrate to contact the ground, but it means the port negative terminal is on the ground plane while the positive terminal is on the patch, both via the same probe conductor.

All other checks (conductor clearances, substrate support containment, excitation collection coverage, port attachment) passed with info-level findings. No blocking issues were found. These are geometric observations only; they do not establish RF performance, impedance match, or resonance.

Assessment complete. The 2×3 inset-fed patch array at 2.45 GHz on FR4 has one actionable warning and several informational findings. The warning: the overhang-union cylinders added to the two rightmost-column elements (row 1 col 3 and row 2 col 3) extend 12.38 mm beyond the substrate edge, creating 309 mm² of unsupported copper. This is a manufacturability/reliability concern—those overhangs have no dielectric support. All six ports show 'attachment unknown' for their positive terminals (geometric coincidence cannot be resolved within the polygonal approximation), but their negative terminals attach cleanly to the ground plane. Several union operations between patch pieces and the overhang tools fall within the curved-boundary approximation uncertainty (info only). Fundamental limitations: these checks are geometry-only—no impedance, resonance, coupling, efficiency, or full-wave RF performance is evaluated. Curved boundaries (cylinders) are approximated polygonal, so near-boundary relationships carry an error bound (~0.13 mm).

The present element pitch (spacing) is **0.55 λ₀** in both the row and column directions. This value comes directly from the `element_spacing_lambda` parameter (0.55) and is confirmed by the engineering.array_spacing analysis, which reports `row_spacing_lambda = 0.55` and `column_spacing_lambda = 0.55` at the design frequency of 2.45 GHz (free-space wavelength λ₀ ≈ 122.36 mm).
